summary: The focused array print depth claim does not require harness maintenance. Every array depth accepted by parsing remains printable under the new guard.

claims.necessity_reason: The harness prints only the tree returned by parsing. Parsing and printing start at depth zero; both array and object parsers reject a container at the same pre-increment depth threshold used by the new array printer. Thus no parser-accepted array triggers the new depth rejection.

before.requirement: Print a parser-produced array at every nesting depth accepted by parsing.
before.reason: The old array printer has no depth rejection, and the harness passes the parsed tree to printing.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Parser dispatch constructs array and object values through their respective parsers.

after.requirement: Print a parser-produced array at every nesting depth accepted by parsing.
after.reason: The new array guard rejects at depth 1000, while array and object parsing reject a container at that same depth. Both print paths begin at depth zero.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Parser dispatch routes every array or object value to its container parser.
Array parsing applies the same pre-increment nesting guard.
Object parsing applies the same guard to mixed nesting.
Ordinary printing initializes depth to zero.
Buffered printing initializes depth to zero.

claims.comparison_reason: The same old harness prints a parser-returned tree on both sides. The added array guard cannot reject an array solely for a nesting depth that parsing accepted.
